candidates.title: MPC Container Ships reports lower Q3 earnings amid fleet renewal
candidates.excerpt: MPC Container Ships (MPCC) reported lower revenue and earnings for the third quarter of 2026, while highlighting firm charter demand, extensive forward coverage and continued progress with its fleet renewal programme. Operating revenue declined to US$113.1 million from US$125.9 million in the same period last year, while EBITDA fell from US$83.5 million to US$69.9 million. Adjusted for non-recurring items, EBITDA reached US$60.8 million, compared with US$74.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted profit decreased to US$36.1 million from US$45 million. Fleet utilisation remained high at 97.8%, slightly above the 97.6% recorded a year earlier. MPCC achieved an adjusted average time charter equivalent rate of US$25,333 per day, compared with US$26,523 per day in the corresponding quarter of 2025. CN updates work to address track issues that led to July 5 derailment in Montreal suburb
candidates.excerpt: MONTREAL — Canadian National will begin increasing passenger train speeds through Repentigny, Quebec, this Friday (Nov. 27) after completing extensive track work at the site of the July 5 derailment in the Montreal suburb. CN said in a statement today (Nov. 25) that it has rebuilt approximately 2,400 feet (750 meters) of track, used more than 2,000 metric tons of crushed stone to reinforce the track foundation, replaced all crossties, and leveled the track. It has also built a new grade crossing and is nearing completion of repairs to a bike path. The 49-car derailment on July 5 caused residents to be evacuated for about five hours while authorities determined that no hazardous materials were spilled [see “CN derailment in Quebec …,” Trains.com, July 6, 2026]. The 172-car train included 13 tank cars containing residue of dangerous goods, according to the Transportation Safety Board of Canada’s preliminary investigation report. candidates.title: Norwood & St. Lawrence locomotive arrives in New York
candidates.excerpt: MADRID, N.Y. — A significant piece of Northern New York’s railroad history has returned home to an enthusiastic community after spending decades in the Steamtown National Historic Site collection. Norwood & St. Lawrence locomotive No. 210 was placed on its new display track at the St. Lawrence Power & Equipment Museum in Madrid on Nov. 20. “I feel elated,” said Roger Austin, the museum’s secretary and a driving force behind the project. “To have it finally come to full fruition is just very satisfying.” Austin worked closely with Steamtown officials to coordinate the transfer of the locomotive, necessary asbestos abatement and wheel repair work, and the truck move from Scranton, Pa., to the Madrid museum. No. 210, an Alco 2-6-0 Mogul, was built in 1923 for the Norwood & St. Lawrence Railroad. candidates.excerpt: It’s been a bit since we’ve seen new tooling for Electro-Motive Corp.’s FT locomotives in HO scale. Rapido Trains’ newest version of the locomotive that is known to have “brought about the demise of the steam engine” showcases smooth running, great looks, and a wealth of railroad-specific detail. The samples we received, provided to Model Railroader free of charge by Rapido Trains, feature plastic and die-cast metal construction, an all-new close-coupling system for greater close-coupled appearance, and full underbody details, including piping and draft gear. As these early diesel engines were often bought as 2,700 horsepower drawbar-connected A-B pairs or 5,400 horsepower A-B-B-A four-unit sets, Rapido offers the models as A-B sets and single B units. Electro-Motive Corp. rolled out its first demonstration set of FTs, which stood for “Freight, Twenty-seven hundred horsepower,” in late November 1939. candidates.title: News photo: Former Wabash Vista-Dome arrives at Branson Scenic
candidates.excerpt: BRANSON, Mo. — The Branson Scenic Railway has added ex-Wabash Railroad Vista-Dome No. 202 to its fleet, according to a Nov. 23 social media post showcasing the car’s arrival at the Branson Depot. No. 202 was built by the Budd Co. in 1950 for the railroad’s Blue Bird, which ran between St. Louis and Chicago. Prior to relocating to the Branson Scenic, the car had been a regular on Lake State Railway’s office car specials in Michigan. Officials from the tourist railroad expect No. 202 to be ready for passenger excursions in 2027 after some mechanical and interior upgrades. — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire@firecrown.com. candidates.title: Weekly U.S. rail traffic remains ahead of 2025 levels
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Continued intermodal strength again kept U.S. weekly rail traffic above 2025 levels for the week ending Nov. 21, 2026. Statistics from the Association of American Railroads show rail traffic for the week was 540,111 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.7% from the same week last year. Included in the overall figure were 235,148 carloads, an increase of 0.5% from the corresponding week in 2025, and 304,963 containers and trailers, a gain of 8.3%. For the year to date, railroads report cumulative volume of 23,711,577 carloads and intermodal units, up 4% from the first 46 weeks of 2025. The 10,536,681 carloads are an increase of 2.7%, while the 13,174,896 intermodal units represent a gain of 5.1%. North American traffic for the week, as reported by nine U.S., Canadian, and Mexican railroads, was 737,413 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.2% from the same week in 2025. candidates.title: TrainsPRO Podcast episode 6 recap
candidates.excerpt: In episode 6 of the TrainsPRO Podcast, Trains Magazine Editor Bill Stephens sits down with intermodal analyst Larry Gross, president and founder of Gross Transportation Consulting. They discuss intermodal’s record year, the growth targets in the proposed Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern merger, and the threat autonomous trucks pose to rail. Gross has more than 40 years of experience in freight transportation, including 27 years at Wabash National, and writes the monthly Landlines column in the Journal of Commerce. What’s driving intermodal’s record year U.S. intermodal is on pace to top its 2018 record. Gross says it’s important to separate intermodal into its two very different markets. International moves ocean containers inland from ports, while domestic moves mostly 53-foot containers. Overall volume is up 3.4% year to date. candidates.title: Opinion: What Conrail has taught us about integration and growth
candidates.excerpt: Trains Turntable: Commentary from Mike McClellan, Norfolk Southern senior vice president and chief strategy officer The Men Who Loved Trains is the definitive book on Northeastern railroading’s fall and rise: From the collapse of Penn Central through the creation of Conrail and Amtrak to the ultimate split of Conrail between Norfolk Southern and CSX in 1999. The book catalogued the challenges and the many opportunities that came with one of the most consequential events in American railroading. Splitting Conrail into two pieces and then integrating the 7,200-mile network into Norfolk Southern and CSX was complex. It is true, early service disruptions frustrated shippers and fueled criticism of the transaction, and this is detailed in the final chapter in the book. While these challenges close the book, it is actually the beginning of the real story. Because integration did stabilize and the benefits did emerge. candidates.title: Imoto Lines deploys new coastal containership Minato
candidates.excerpt: Japanese domestic carrier Imoto Lines has deployed the newly built containership Minato on its western Japan service. The vessel was launched on 17 August and is owned by Fukuyoshi Kaiun. It was constructed by Koike Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering as the third vessel in the Maya class, following the delivery of the first ship in 2024. Although Imoto Lines describes Minato as a 200 TEU-class vessel, its stated maximum container capacity is 245 TEU, including space for 42 refrigerated containers. The ship made its inaugural call at the Port of Kobe on 24 November, where a welcoming ceremony was held. Representatives from the Kobe City Port and Harbor Bureau and Hanshin Port presented commemorative gifts to Captain Tadahiro Yabuta. Minato measures 96.81 metres in length and 14 metres in width. candidates.title: APM Terminals and Port of Rotterdam prepare terminal expansion
candidates.excerpt: APM Terminals Maasvlakte II and the Port of Rotterdam Authority are preparing a new phase of expansion at the Maasvlakte II container terminal. It will add 25 hectares of terminal area, about 711 metres of additional quay and supporting port infrastructure, and is expected to raise annual capacity by roughly 1.4 million TEU once complete. The terminal has been investing in its facilities at Prinses Amaliahaven since 2008, and the expansion is being delivered in phases while the existing terminal stays fully operational. The first part has recently come into service. The two organisations will divide the work. APM Terminals Maasvlakte II will concentrate on developing terminal operations, while the Port of Rotterdam Authority, in cooperation with the terminal, will prepare the site for construction and deliver the maritime infrastructure. candidates.title: PIL and Qingdao Port complete China’s first bio-LNG bunkering for international shipping
candidates.excerpt: Pacific International Lines (PIL) and Qingdao Port have completed what they describe as China’s first liquefied bio-methane (LBM) bunkering operation for an internationally trading vessel. The operation took place at Qingdao Port’s QQCTN terminal, where PIL’s LNG dual-fuel containership Kota Odyssey received ISCC-certified LBM through a truck-to-ship transfer. It also marks the Singapore-based carrier’s first use of the renewable fuel in its fleet. Produced from organic feedstocks, LBM, also known as bio-LNG, can be used in LNG dual-fuel engines without modifying the vessels’ existing machinery. PIL is introducing the fuel as part of its efforts to reduce shipping emissions while expanding its fleet of dual-fuel containerships. According to the carrier, the batch supplied at Qingdao is expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by more than 70% compared with conventional fuel oil, based on a well-to-wake lifecycle assessment. candidates.excerpt: Oslo-listed MPC Container Ships (MPCC) has revealed $76.3m in secondhand transactions, buying a modern feeder and selling two older containerships while locking in fresh employment for two vessels. The Constantin Baack-led owner has confirmed a $35.4m deal for a 2019-built 1,800 teu containership, brokers earlier identified as Nordmaas from Germany’s Reederei Nord fleet. The Yangzijiang-built vessel is due to join MPCC in December under the name AS Silvie and has already been fixed forward for 28 to 31 months at $25,500 per day, starting in April next year. MPCC has also fixed the 2006-built, 2,800 teu AS Carolina for 35 to 36 months at $29,900 per day, with the new charter kicking in during the first quarter of 2027. On the sales front, the company has confirmed deals to offload the 2008-built AS Sicilia for $28.9m and the 2004-built AS Freya for $12m. candidates.excerpt: WSC report highlights global renewable marine fuel opportunities as dual-fuel fleet set to meet 20% of liner energy demand by 2030 By around 2030, ships already operating or on order that are capable of using renewable marine fuels are expected to account for more than one-fifth of liner shipping’s total energy demand, demonstrating the scale of potential demand for renewable fuels. However, investment in ships alone will not deliver the energy transition. Without binding global regulations that close the price gap between conventional and renewable fuels, the demand these ships represent risks going unrealised, holding back investment in renewable fuel production and supply infrastructure. candidates.excerpt: Return of container shipping to Suez Canal is causing European port congestion and impacting Asia-UK shipments, says Davies Turner Davies Turner, one of the UK’s largest independent freight forwarding and logistics companies, says that disruption to container shipments from Asia to the UK following the return of more container shipping lines to the Suez Canal routing, is leading to increased congestion at major European ports and delays to some UK-bound cargo. candidates.title: Ignite bolsters lending team with ThinCats hires
candidates.excerpt: Ignite bolsters lending team with ThinCats hires UK lender Ignite Funding Partners has made two senior appointments, adding credit and origination expertise weeks after its launch. The firm has hired David Jamieson as chief credit partner and Steven Munt as senior funding partner. Jamieson will lead credit across Ignite’s four lending strategies: sponsors, owner-managed businesses, healthcare and fund finance. He joins from ThinCats, where he was head of credit and sat on the investment committee, focusing on the sponsor and healthcare lending book. Munt, who will be responsible for originating new lending opportunities across London and the south, also joins from ThinCats, where he was senior director of business development. He previously held senior roles at Shawbrook Bank, Lloyds and RBS. candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic rose 7.3% in the week ending November 14, 2026, compared with the same week last year, as double-digit intermodal growth outpaced gains in conventional carload shipments, according to the Association of American Railroads. Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains. Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%. The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%.
